user_input: How do you use vba to send an email
model_output:
You can use VBA (Visual Basic for Applications) to send an email in Microsoft Outlook by recording a macro. Here are the steps:
1. Open Microsoft Outlook and press "Alt + F11" to open the Visual Basic Editor.
2. In the Project Explorer, expand the "Microsoft Outlook Objects" folder and double-click on "ThisOutlookSession".
3. In the code editor, go to the "Tools" menu and select "References". Check the box next to "Microsoft Outlook xx.x Object Library" (where "xx.x" is the version of Outlook you are using).
4. Go back to the code editor and add the following code:
```vbnet
Sub SendEmail()
  Dim olApp As Outlook.Application
  Set olApp = New Outlook.Application
  Dim olMail As Outlook.MailItem
  Set olMail = olApp.CreateItem(0)
  olMail.To = "recipient@example.com"
  olMail.Subject = "The subject of the email"
  olMail.Body = "The body of the email"
  olMail.Send
  Set olMail = Nothing
  Set olApp = Nothing
End Sub
```
5. Save the code and close the Visual Basic Editor. To run the macro, go back to Outlook and press "Alt + F8" to open the "Macro" dialog box. Select "SendEmail" and click "Run".

Note: This code creates a new email and sends it to the recipient specified in the "To" field. You can modify the code to include additional fields and to specify the email account to use.
